script:
Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Friday, November 20. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 7 degrees Celsius, light rain. The high will be 16 and the low 6 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 45 percent.

You have no appointments scheduled in the next 24 hours.

Now, the top 5 stories in AI today.

First, from The Verge: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer. Google's Gemini app for macOS now includes computer use, allowing the AI to help users complete multi-step tasks across local files, desktop applications, and the web. Google suggests the feature can speed up workflows, fill in forms, create presentations, and list items for sale. Users will need to grant permissions for the AI to access their computer. Why it matters: Brings agent-like computer control directly to Mac desktops, expanding practical AI agent capabilities to mainstream consumer operating systems.

Second, from The Verge: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent. Apple is hiring an engineer to lead development of its own agentic AI assistant, according to a job listing spotted by Bloomberg. The agent would be capable of browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services to perform a range of tasks. The role involves creating an assistant that can act on behalf of users across multiple domains. Why it matters: Signals Apple's entry into the autonomous AI agent space, potentially reshaping how Apple users interact with devices and services.

Third, from Google: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API. Google has introduced Tool Retrieval in preview for the Gemini API, enabling developers to give agents access to hundreds of tools while using fewer tokens. The feature is designed to make agent development more efficient by reducing token consumption when accessing extensive toolsets. The preview allows agents to retrieve and use tools dynamically without loading all of them at once. Why it matters: Lowers the cost and complexity of building capable AI agents by providing broad tool access with improved token efficiency for developers.

Fourth, from WIRED: Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents. Google built a giant alternate-universe internet—a massive sandbox—to train Chrome AI browsing agents without risking them going rogue on the live web. The mirror dimension allows the Chrome team to properly test AI agents in a realistic but contained environment. The sandbox replicates internet conditions so agents can be trained and evaluated before deployment to real users. Why it matters: Represents significant infrastructure investment in safe AI agent development and testing at scale for autonomous browsing capabilities.

Fifth, from TechCrunch: Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO. Anthropic's seven founders each pocketed $280 million, totaling nearly $2 billion, at an upgraded IPO price of $83 per share. The company reached a valuation of nearly $105 billion in what is described as a record-breaking IPO. Related coverage indicates the Public Benefit Foundation and employee donations could direct up to $156 billion to charity at a $95 stock price. Why it matters: One of the largest AI company IPOs in history, marking a major financial milestone for the AI industry and Anthropic's investors.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
